fichas.title: Lighting parameters and illuminance values
fichas.summary: Explains luminous flux, luminous intensity, illuminance, and luminance, and lists example illuminance levels from global radiation to moonlight. Luminance is associated with perceived brightness and potential glare; shading of lamps is therefore required in interiors.
uses: Inform lighting design and glare control

dimensions.label: Global radiation (clear sky), maximum illuminance
dimensions.context: Maximum illuminance listed for global radiation under a clear sky.

dimensions.label: Global radiation (cloudy sky), maximum illuminance
dimensions.context: Maximum illuminance listed for global radiation under a cloudy sky.

fichas.title: Artificial lighting: lamp types and performance
fichas.summary: Describes artificial lighting sources as lamps used with fittings, which hold the lamp and distribute light. Classifies sources into filament and discharge lamps. Filament lamps produce substantial heat radiation and relatively little visible light; halogen filament lamps are compact and suitable for narrow-beam spotlights. The page also illustrates lamp categories and gives examples of lamp power ratings.
uses: Provide general or directed artificial lighting
Assess lamp efficacy, lifetime, and electrical supply requirements

dimensions.label: Visible-light share of energy produced by filament lamps
dimensions.context: Approximate proportion of energy produced that is visible light; most is heat radiation.

dimensions.label: Filament-lamp luminous efficacy
dimensions.context: Typical low luminous efficacy of filament lamps.

dimensions.label: Filament-lamp lifetime
dimensions.ocr_raw: short lifetime of lamps at about 1000 hours

dimensions.label: Halogen filament-lamp luminous efficacy
dimensions.context: Upper value stated for halogen lamps, compared with simple light bulbs.
